lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: point, line, distance, and arc as undefined starting terms
lessonRef.title: Reteach and varied practice: point, line, distance, and arc as undefined starting terms

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: These two examples show the same idea in two different formats.

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle. Central angle per side?
Why does the equilateral triangle construction work?

workedSolution.answer: All three sides equal the radius

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a perpendicular lines?
choices: two lines that intersect to form right angles
two lines with opposite slopes
two lines that form an isosceles triangle
two lines that never meet

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Through point P not on line ℓ, copy the angle that a transversal makes with ℓ, placing the copy at P on the same transversal. What has been constructed?
choices: a line through P perpendicular to ℓ
the reflection of ℓ across P
a line through P parallel to ℓ
the perpendicular bisector of the transversal

items.prompt: A regular quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle of radius 12. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the angle bisector construction?
choices: The ray drawn appears to split the angle evenly.
The construction relies on the angle being acute.
The construction builds two congruent triangles by SSS, so the angles at the vertex are congruent.
Equal arcs always produce equal angles regardless of the triangle.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a angle?
choices: a corner of a polygon
the space between two intersecting lines
the figure formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint
the amount of turn measured in degrees

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. With the compass set to the radius, mark successive arcs around the circle from a starting point, then join consecutive marks. What has been constructed?
choices: a square inscribed in the circle
an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle
a regular hexagon inscribed in the circle
a regular pentagon inscribed in the circle

items.prompt: A regular quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle of radius 3. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the equilateral triangle construction on a given segment?
choices: Both circles have radius equal to the segment, so all three sides are that same length.
The circles intersect, which guarantees 60° angles by definition.
The intersection point is the midpoint of the segment.
The construction works only when the segment is horizontal.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a circle?
choices: the set of all points in a plane at a fixed distance from a given centre point
a polygon with infinitely many sides
a closed curve with no corners
a shape whose area is πr²
